# Cornell University Overview
Cornell University, founded in 1865 in Ithaca, New York, is a prominent private and public research university recognized as New York's land-grant institution. The main Ithaca campus spans 745 acres and features a blend of historic and modern architecture, with several buildings listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Cornell also operates campuses in New York City, including Weill Cornell Medicine and Cornell Tech, as well as the Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar. The university’s organization is highly decentralized, comprising 16 colleges—four statutory SUNY-supported colleges and 12 privately endowed colleges—that exercise autonomy over academics and admissions. As of 2024, Cornell's endowment is $10.7 billion, placing it among the largest in the U.S., and it consistently receives record-breaking philanthropic donations supporting research, sustainability, and academic initiatives.
Cornell is recognized for its rigorous admissions, with a 6.9% acceptance rate for the Class of 2026 and highly competitive standardized test scores. The student body is diverse and economically varied, with need-blind admissions for U.S. applicants and robust financial aid programs. Academically, Cornell offers a vast array of undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs, including internationally focused majors and study abroad opportunities. The university is classified as an R1 research institution, ranking 14th nationally in R&D expenditures. Cornell has contributed significantly to science, engineering, computing, and medicine, and operates numerous research facilities and off-campus study programs. The Cornell University Library system, with over 10 million holdings, supports its research and scholarship, and the university maintains active student life through over 1,000 organizations, Greek life, student government, robust music, outdoor education, athletics programs, and a strong tradition of campus lore. Notable alumni and faculty include Nobel laureates, heads of state, and leading figures across disciplines, with a global reputation reflected in top-tier rankings and sustained academic excellence.
